citation_short: Huang Wang & Sun. Are long corolla tubes in Pedicularis driven by pollinator selection?
manipulation: P. tricolor corolla tube shortened by bending tube and fixing with clear sticky tape; P. siphonantha tube length varied under watering/shading
design_or_sample: P. tricolor: 12 flowering individuals; first arrivals to 72 shortened and 72 unmanipulated flowers; seed-set analysis F1,180. P. siphonantha: 25 plants in experimental plot plus 45 open-pollinated flowers.
response: bumblebee visitation; seed set; corolla tube length
key_result: P. tricolor visits/census shortened 2.70±0.34 vs control 2.61±0.37, P=0.857; seed set 0.45±0.022 vs 0.48±0.018, P=0.262
method_relevance: Strong congeneric non-destructive floral-dimension manipulation and sham/control feasibility precedent for P0.
notes: Supports manipulation family and off-target/visitor checks; does not validate realized exsertion manipulation in P. rex.

citation_short: Yang Sun & Guo. Resource limitation and pollen source affecting seed production in two louseworts
manipulation: Open pollination with supplemental self or outcross pollen; separate hand self/outcross pollination on bagged flowers
design_or_sample: Natural-population supplementation and bagged hand-pollination experiments; exact sample sizes not recovered from indexed abstract.
response: stigmatic pollen load; seed production per capsule; pollen limitation
key_result: Additional self/outcross pollen did not increase seed production in the open-pollination supplementation test; bagged hand self vs outcross treatments differed in seed production.
method_relevance: Direct congeneric precedent for adding self/outcross pollen and measuring seed-production response without inventing a new P1 treatment family.
notes: Method precedent only. Species differ from P. rex and reported lack of supplementation response is not a P. rex expected effect.

citation_short: Dai Kadiori Wang & Yang. Pollen limitation plasticity and mixed mating in Pedicularis siphonantha
manipulation: Supplemental hand pollination with outcross pollen across altitude populations; self/outcross/control mating treatments described in full-text version
design_or_sample: Four large populations from 3200-4300 m; indexed full-text copy describes 20 randomly selected individuals per population with three marked flowers for natural/self/outcross treatments.
response: seed production per capsule; fruit set; pollen limitation; floral traits
key_result: Outcross supplementation significantly increased seed production per capsule in high-altitude populations but not lower-altitude populations.
method_relevance: Congeneric paired-within-plant supplementation precedent and evidence that supplementation effect is context-dependent.
notes: Use for P1 design structure and heterogeneity expectation; do not borrow its effect as a P. rex CAL-B target.

citation_short: Huang & Shi. Floral isolation in Pedicularis
target_stage: CAL_A; P1 method handling; exclusion/sham logic
manipulation: Galea gap or tip blocked with glue; open pollination or pollinator exclusion by small nylon nets
design_or_sample: 10 plants per species; on each plant three flowers assigned to gap-blocked/open, tip-blocked/open, or tip-blocked/bagged; pilot tested glue brands and found manipulated flowers were not discriminated by bumblebees.
response: pollen grains remaining at gap/tip; bee-body pollen placement; stigma contact
key_result: Tip-blocked open flowers retained far more tip pollen than pollinator-excluded flowers in all eight species (all P<0.001); manipulation pilot reported no bumblebee discrimination.
method_relevance: Strong Pedicularis precedent for flower-level handling controls, physical blocking, bagging/exclusion and explicit visitor-discrimination checks.
notes: Not a pollen-supplementation effect and not seed-predator exclusion; useful method-control precedent only.

citation_short: Sun & Huang. Rainwater in cupulate bracts repels seed herbivores
manipulation: Bract water drained vs intact control; visitor censuses and seed outcomes
design_or_sample: Six populations; 40-60 tagged individuals/population; 20-30 drained individuals/population; >=6 capsules/individual; Shama visitor plots included five drained and five intact plots.
response: pollinator and nectar-robber visitation; initial/final seed set; seed predation
key_result: Drainage changed seed predation/final seed outcome while no detected treatment effect occurred for pollinator visit rate or initial seed set.
method_relevance: Same-species precedent for testing antagonist-related intervention selectivity and measuring contamination endpoints.
notes: Water drainage remains deprecated as SCH independent G. It supports handling/selectivity logic and BITA-y, not the current predator-exclusion intervention.
